decisions.descriptionMarkdown:
One release unit for the repository. `release-plz.toml` runs git-only (`git_only = true`, `publish = false`). `dtcg_runtime` owns the tag `v{{ version }}`, the GitHub Release (`git_release_enable = true`: release-plz creates it; there is no cargo-dist here) and the root changelog (`changelog_path = "./CHANGELOG.md"`, `changelog_include = ["dtcg_runtime_derive"]`). `dtcg_runtime_derive` shares `version_group = "dtcg"` with tag, release and changelog off, and inherits the workspace `git_tag_name`. `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"` and `semver_check = false` (d-stay-on-1x). `[changelog]` is RayX.CLI's section with this library's header and the `Migration:` footer line of d-changelog-from-commits.

Proof: `check-release-preview` runs release-plz 0.3.172 and cargo-semver-checks 0.51 (the versions `release-plz/action@v0.5` installs) in a scratch copy of the working tree: the first-release dry run, then `release-plz update` after a docs-only commit (no release), a derive fix (`1.0.1`), a `feat` that states a break with a `Migration:` footer (`1.1.0`, footer rendered), and a fix that removes a public function (`1.0.1`, no API check although cargo-semver-checks is installed).
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- One tag `vX.Y.Z`, one GitHub Release and one root `CHANGELOG.md` section per version; never a `dtcg_runtime_derive-v*` tag or a per-crate changelog.
- Both crates always carry the same version (`version.workspace = true` plus the version group).
- Nothing is published: `publish = false` here, `git_only` (release-plz rejects `publish = true` with it); the manifests stay crates.io-ready.
- `dtcg_runtime_derive` keeps the inherited `git_tag_name`; overriding it would hide `v*` tags from its previous-version lookup.
- The preview never runs in the repository: it copies the working tree to a temp directory, deletes the copy's tags and disables its push URL.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown:
Facts from release-plz's source at 0.3.172 (read during planning): in git-only mode each package's previous version is the highest tag matching its own `git_tag_name` template, whether or not it creates tags (`next_ver.rs`, `process_git_only_package`), so the derive crate finds `v1.0.0` through the inherited template, and no matching tag means an initial release. The tagged workspace is reconstructed from a git worktree without packaging ("creating archives would require registry versions even for dependencies that will never be published"), so the unpublished derive dependency is no obstacle. One workspace tag shared by several packages is covered by the test `git_only_update_handles_packages_sharing_a_release_tag`, semver checks in git-only mode by `git_only_checks_semver_with_versionless_private_dependencies`. Only `lib`/`rlib`/`dylib` targets would be semver-checked (`updater.rs`, `contains_library`); a missing cargo-semver-checks only logs a warning, so the preview demands it on PATH to make its "no API check with `semver_check = false`" proof meaningful (CI's action installs it). A dry-run release logs `<package> <version>: due to dry, skipping the following: ["creation of tag 'v1.0.0'", "creation of git release"]` or `no release method enabled` (`release.rs`, `log_dry_run_info`).

`release_commits` is the CLI's `^(feat|fix|perf)`: under the 1.x policy breaking work is typed `feat`, so the earlier any-type-breaking alternative is gone (amendment 1 A). One version group rather than independent versions: both crates inherit `[workspace.package] version` and `dtcg_runtime` re-exports the derive macros, so they are one product. Mirroring RayX.CLI's tool versions in the preview keeps the local proof equal to what CI will run.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: 1.x policy (owner, amendment 1 A): the owner is the only consumer, so the crates stay on `1.x`. No commit is marked breaking: no `!` after the type or scope and no `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. A breaking change is committed as `feat` (minor), or `fix` when it is a fix, with the break stated in the body and `Migration:` footers (d-changelog-from-commits). `semver_check = false` and `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"`. Before a release PR is merged, its proposed version must still be `1.x`; a `2.0.0` proposal means a stray `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:`, and that commit is reworded (force push allowed) instead of merging. The policy ends when a second consumer appears; then `!` and major bumps return.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- No release of this epic or after it proposes `2.0.0` while the policy holds.
- The preview proves both halves: a break-describing `feat` gives `1.1.0`; an API removal under `fix` gives `1.0.1` with cargo-semver-checks installed.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: release-plz has no option to cap a major bump: it bumps the major for a `!` commit, a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer, or an API break found by cargo-semver-checks (release-plz.dev/docs/semver-check). Turning all three off is the only way to stay on 1.x; the release-PR version check catches a mistake before it becomes a tag the ruleset makes permanent. RayX.CLI and the other libraries follow the same policy through their own amendments.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: Clean start at 1.0.0: `[workspace.package] version` and both own-crate requirements in `[workspace.dependencies]` (including the `dtcg_runtime` entry no member uses) become `1.0.0`; `Cargo.lock` follows (`cargo update --workspace --offline`). `CHANGELOG.md` becomes the configured header plus `## [1.0.0] - <date>` above the former `[Unreleased]` content, unchanged, and nothing else. The date is the release push's day: written when the version commit is made, corrected in t09 if the release push happens later.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- Crate manifests are untouched: versions inherited, the derive crate's dev-dependency on `dtcg_runtime` path-only.
- The 1.0.0 section is the hand-written history, kept verbatim; generated sections start with the next release.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: release-plz keeps an existing changelog header verbatim (`changelog_parser::parse_header`: everything through an `## [Unreleased]` heading, else everything before the first `## `) and inserts each new section directly after it, so the file must already start with the configured header and must not end it with an Unreleased heading. The GitHub Release notes are the body of the newest versioned section (`last_changes` skips Unreleased), so the 1.0.0 notes are exactly the former Unreleased text. RayX.CLI's v1.0.0 took the same route (hand-written `## [1.0.0]`, tagged by the git-only initial release).

decisions.descriptionMarkdown:
From 1.0.0 on, release-plz writes `CHANGELOG.md` from Conventional Commits; feature commits no longer edit it. Migration notes go into `Migration:` footers: a change a consumer must react to is committed under the 1.x policy (d-stay-on-1x) as `feat(scope): …` (or `fix`) whose body states the break and whose last paragraph carries one or more `Migration:` footers naming each affected consumer and what to change (for example `Migration: RayX: rename … in crates/rayx_theme/…`, `Migration: RayX.TokenEditor: …`). The changelog template loops over git-cliff's `commit.footers` and prints each `Migration` footer as an indented `Migration: <value>` line under the entry, so the per-consumer migration reaches the changelog and the GitHub Release. A line that reads badly is fixed on the release PR right before it is merged.

The doctest half of the superseded decision carries over unchanged: `lib.rs` includes `README.md` and every guide chapter in `#[cfg(doctest)]` modules, every code block is language-tagged, and an API or behaviour change updates the affected chapter examples in the same commit.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- `CHANGELOG.md` changes only through release-plz (release PR), the version commit of this epic, or the documented by-hand fallback.
- No `!` and no `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer (they force a major bump); the migration footer token is exactly `Migration`.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: The current decision (2026-10-07) makes every behaviour change hand-edit `CHANGELOG.md`, including a Migration subsection per consumer. With generated sections such hand edits would land beside or under release-plz's output (it inserts below the header and never merges Unreleased text), so the migration moves into the commit as a Conventional Commits footer. It is a `Migration:` footer rather than `BREAKING CHANGE:` because release-plz bumps the major for `BREAKING CHANGE:` and cannot cap it (amendment 1 A). release-plz closes a release PR that carries human commits once `main` moves on, so editing the release PR is a final touch, not a workflow.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown:
`.github/workflows/release-plz.yml` is RayX.CLI's workflow with this repository's guard and `ci.yml`'s checkout major; it runs no tests. `ci.yml` stays unchanged: `pull_request` plus `push: main`, one short fmt/clippy/test/wasm/package job on Ubuntu and Windows, which is also all a release PR runs.

First release order: s1 and s2 (1.0.0 manifests, changelog, release config, docs) are pushed first without the workflow, so nothing is tagged and `ci.yml` proves that code on `main`. After verifying the owner prerequisites (the push itself is pre-approved, amendment 1 D), t09 pushes the workflow commit (plus the date fix if the day changed); the `release` job tags `v1.0.0` on that push, a commit whose code `ci.yml` already passed.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- `release-plz.yml` never lands before the 1.0.0 version (it would tag `0.1.0`) and is not pushed before OWN-1 and OWN-2 are verified and `ci.yml` passed the pushed s1–s2 commits on `main`.
- `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` is the workflow's only secret, used for checkout and as `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Tags come only from release-plz or the documented by-hand fallback.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: Events made with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` start no workflows, so with it the release PR would get no CI. Amendment 1 B confirms light CI on pushes; this is a deviation from the CLI decision's invariant "`ci.yml` stays pull-request only; `release-plz.yml` is the one workflow that runs on pushes to `main`": RayX.CLI merges implementation through pull requests, while this repository's owner policy pushes implementation straight to `main`, and dropping `ci.yml`'s push trigger would leave those commits untested. A release PR costs one existing 2.5-to-4-minute job on two hosts; there is nothing heavier to filter (no e2e, performance or lane suites), so no paths filter is added. The two-push first release puts the tag on code `ci.yml` already passed, instead of tagging while the only CI run is still going; RayX.CLI's first release (2026-10-14, tag on the push, no release PR opened) shows git-only release-plz tags an untagged `1.0.0` directly.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: Consumers depend on a release tag, `dtcg_runtime = { git = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.Dtcg", tag = "vX.Y.Z" }`, in every place that shows how to depend on the crate (README, chapter 2, chapter 14, `docs/releasing.md`, `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`); `Cargo.lock` records the commit and tag bumps are by hand. A change RayX needs is released here first, then RayX bumps its tag and validates its affected crates and Test Suite specs: no paired commits, no relative path, no local override. Examples name `v1.0.0` and point at the Releases page for the latest tag.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- No documentation recommends an unpinned git dependency, a branch, a path or crates.io.
- Consumers depend on `dtcg_runtime` only; it re-exports the derive macros, and the derive crate resolves from the same tag.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: Owner decisions 1, 2 and 6 (2026-10-18). RayX still builds against `../RayX.Dtcg` until its epic `rayx-released-libraries` switches to the tag; these documents state the contract that epic makes true. The repository rules "pair a public API change that RayX uses with the matching RayX commit" (`knowledge/repository/rules.md`) and "not proven until RayX's affected crates and Test Suite specs pass against it" (`knowledge/repository/validation/rules.md`) become "release first, then RayX bumps its tag and validates"; they are rules, not decisions, and are synced when this epic's decisions are promoted.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: `docs/releasing.md` is the maintainer page, modelled on RayX.CLI's `docs/releasing.md` without cargo-dist (release-plz creates the GitHub Release here). Chapter 14's Releases section summarises it and links it; the README Development section may link it too. It is not a guide chapter, so it is not added to the `#[cfg(doctest)]` documentation module in `crates/dtcg_runtime/src/lib.rs` (nothing under `crates/` changes); its code blocks still carry non-Rust tags (`bash`, `toml`, `json`, `text`).
decisions.invariantsMarkdown: - Every code block in README and `docs/*.md` carries a language tag.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: The guide chapters are user documentation compiled as doctests; release mechanics are for maintainers and contain no Rust. Keeping them in one page with the same shape across the four libraries is what makes the template reusable.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: The owner completed the prerequisites on 2026-10-18 (amendment 1 C): the repository secret `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` (the PAT RayX.CLI uses) and the tag ruleset "Release tags" (`refs/tags/v*`; `update`, `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`; no bypass; tag creation allowed). The epic verifies both read-only (`check-release-secret` lists secret names only, `check-tag-ruleset` reads the rulesets) and never creates, changes or handles them. Whether the PAT can reach RayX.Dtcg shows only in the first Release-plz run; on a checkout or push failure t09 reports to the owner (fix: add the repository to the PAT) instead of retrying.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- Tag creation stays allowed (release-plz pushes tags as the token's owner); only updates, deletions and non-fast-forward moves are blocked.
- The agent never reads, prints or sets a secret value.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: Both were confirmed read-only while amending (secret updated 2026-10-18T21:09:25Z; ruleset 25358677 active with no bypass). The PAT was created for "only RayX.CLI"; if its repository access was not extended, nothing local can detect it, so the first run is the proof. The existing branch ruleset `DefaultRules` blocks deletion and non-fast-forward pushes on `main` with an always-bypass for the owner's account `dXnSix`, so the force-with-lease push policy works with the owner's credentials.
